intervention_label: EUS-guided core biopsy of the recurrent pancreatic body mass
access_summary: Routine at any high-volume pancreas center and the single gate in front of almost everything else in this dossier: trial screening, CLDN18.2 re-staining, and re-sequencing all want current tissue. The likely vascular invasion around the mass can complicate the needle path, so this belongs with an experienced pancreaticobiliary endosonographer, and the passes should be planned up front to yield cores for DNA+RNA NGS plus IHC, not just cytology.
next_steps: Book EUS with fine-needle biopsy (FNB, core needle) at a high-volume pancreaticobiliary center; flag the vascular involvement on the referral so the endosonographer plans the approach.
Specify on the requisition that cores are needed for comprehensive DNA+RNA NGS, CLDN18.2 IHC, and confirmation of PDAC histology; ask the endosonographer to take enough passes for all three.
If the mass proves unsafe to biopsy, fall back to the ctDNA liquid panel (separate row) and the archival 2025 resection block for CLDN18.2 re-staining.
payer_access_notes: EUS biopsy of a suspected recurrence is standard diagnostic care and routinely covered; no special authorization pathway applies.
geographic_scope: US, routine at academic and large community centers
notes: Biopsy also settles whether the recurrence is treated as locally recurrent or metastatic disease, which changes which trials and the daraxonrasib EAP this patient can reach.

intervention_label: Comprehensive DNA+RNA NGS on the recurrence with codon-level KRAS
access_summary: Commercially available from multiple CLIA labs (FoundationOne CDx, Tempus xT/xR, Caris MI Profile) and orderable by any oncologist; all of these report KRAS at codon level, which matters here because G12R gates which RAS programs the patient fits. The constraint is tissue: the recurrence has to be biopsied first, and the lab needs adequate tumor content from the cores.
next_steps: Order a comprehensive DNA+RNA panel on the recurrence cores as soon as the biopsy is done; confirm the requisition asks for codon-level KRAS, TP53, and fusion calling.
Ask the lab to hold residual tissue rather than exhaust the block, since CLDN18.2 IHC and possible sponsor central labs will want sections too.
Have the report sent to whoever runs trial screening so the G12R and Y220C persistence calls flow straight into eligibility packets.
payer_access_notes: Medicare covers FDA-approved comprehensive NGS for advanced or recurrent cancer under NCD 90.2; commercial payers broadly follow. Labs run financial-assistance programs when prior authorization stalls.
geographic_scope: US, mail-in from any treating center

intervention_label: ctDNA comprehensive liquid panel (Guardant360 CDx or FoundationOne Liquid CDx)
access_summary: A blood draw orderable now, before any biopsy, and the route to confirming that KRAS G12R and TP53 Y220C persist in the recurrence if tissue proves hard to get. Several protocols in this dossier accept ctDNA documentation of the target variant, so the same report doubles as trial-entry evidence. The caveat is sensitivity: a small, mostly local recurrence can shed little ctDNA, so a negative result does not exclude persistence.

manufacturer.company: Guardant Health (Guardant360 CDx); Foundation Medicine (FoundationOne Liquid CDx)
manufacturer.notes: Phone and email are Guardant client services, captured from the FDA-posted Guardant360 CDx labeling. Foundation Medicine orders go through the treating center's existing Foundation account or foundationmedicine.com.

next_steps: Order the liquid panel at the next clinic visit; it does not need to wait for the EUS.
If tissue biopsy is deferred or fails, use the ctDNA report as the variant-persistence document for Y220C and G12R trial screening.
Repeat or upgrade to tissue NGS once cores exist, since IHC targets like CLDN18.2 cannot be read from blood.
payer_access_notes: Both FDA-approved liquid panels are covered by Medicare under NCD 90.2 for advanced/recurrent cancer; both companies run patient-assistance billing programs.
geographic_scope: US, blood draw at any treating center

intervention_label: CLDN18.2 re-stain on the FDA companion-diagnostic assay (VENTANA CLDN18 43-14A RxDx)
access_summary: The FDA-approved 43-14A CDx assay is available as a send-out from at least three US reference labs, so re-staining the archival 2025 resection block can happen this week without waiting for a biopsy. NeoGenomics runs it in 1 to 2 days, Labcorp Oncology (test 452390) in about 3, and Mayo Clinic Laboratories lists it as test CLD18. We could not confirm that Tempus or Caris offer the 43-14A CDx assay, which matches what the target validator found, so route the order to one of the three verified labs. The prior 60% 2+/3+ call was on an unstated clone; the CDx re-stain settles where this tumor really sits against the 75% zolbetuximab cutoff and the lower trial cutoffs (FG-M108's phase 3 uses 40% or more at 2+ or higher).

manufacturer.company: NeoGenomics (test 'Claudin 18 FDA (VYLOY)'); Labcorp Oncology (test 452390); Mayo Clinic Laboratories (test CLD18 / 620665)
manufacturer.notes: Phone is NeoGenomics client services (option 3), listed on the test page; TAT 1-2 days, tech-only in 24 hours. Labcorp page: https://oncology.labcorp.com/tests/452390/claudin-18-ihc (TAT 3 days). Mayo page: https://www.mayocliniclabs.com/test-catalog/overview/620665.

next_steps: Send the December 2025 resection block (or 5 unstained slides) to NeoGenomics or Labcorp now; the archival stain is informative even before the recurrence is biopsied.
When recurrence cores exist, repeat the stain on current tissue, since CAR-T and ADC sponsors often require it and expression can shift after chemotherapy.
File both reports with the percentage at 2+/3+ stated explicitly, so each CLDN18.2 program's cutoff can be checked without re-review.
payer_access_notes: IHC on archival tissue is routinely covered as pathology; the FDA CDx billing code is established through the zolbetuximab approval.
geographic_scope: US send-out from any pathology department
notes: Note the assay reads total CLDN18 (both isoforms) via the C-terminus; in gastric and pancreatic tumors CLDN18.2 is the dominant isoform, which is why the CDx works.

intervention_label: Dedicated germline multigene panel (BRCA1/2, PALB2, ATM); BRACAnalysis CDx is the olaparib companion diagnostic
access_summary: Guidelines recommend germline testing for every pancreatic cancer patient, and the incidental tumor-NGS reporting this case currently relies on does not rule those genes out. Myriad's BRACAnalysis CDx is the FDA companion diagnostic tied to the olaparib pancreatic indication and returns results in about 14 days; a broader multigene panel (Invitae, Ambry, Myriad MyRisk) covers PALB2 and ATM as well. The result gates the entire PARP and platinum-emphasis branch of this dossier.

manufacturer.notes: Phone is Myriad's billing and coverage line from the BRACAnalysis CDx patient guide. Ordering is via requisition form or the Myriad provider portal.

next_steps: Order the germline panel now; it is a blood or saliva test and does not depend on the biopsy.
If a BRCA1/2 pathogenic variant returns, order or confirm BRACAnalysis CDx specifically, since it is the assay named in the olaparib label.
Route any positive to genetic counseling, both for treatment gating and for family implications.
payer_access_notes: Broadly covered for pancreatic cancer under NCCN-aligned payer policies; Myriad states most appropriate patients pay nothing out of pocket.
geographic_scope: US, blood/saliva kit from any clinic

intervention_label: Oxaliplatin neuropathy grading and baseline organ-function labs
access_summary: A clinic-visit item, not a procurement problem: CTCAE grading of the residual neuropathy after 10 FOLFIRINOX cycles plus CBC, CMP, bilirubin, and creatinine clearance. Nearly every protocol in this dossier requires labs within 7 to 28 days of first dose and many cap neuropathy at grade 1, so having current numbers on file is what lets a screening call turn into a screening visit.
next_steps: Grade the neuropathy formally (CTCAE v5) at the next visit and put the grade in the chart where trial screeners will find it.
Draw baseline CBC, CMP, bilirubin, INR/PTT, and calculate creatinine clearance; repeat within the window a target protocol specifies.
Document post-Whipple pancreatic enzyme use and nutritional status, since some protocols ask about absorption for oral agents.
payer_access_notes: Routine evaluation and management; no access barrier.

access_summary: Two live routes, and the expanded-access one is real: FDA authorized Revolution Medicines' EAP (protocol RMC-6236-401, NCT07573215) in May 2026 for previously treated metastatic PDAC, with dozens of US sites listed as available and drug supplied free of charge; the NDA was accepted for FDA review in July 2026. RASolute 302 is closed to enrollment, but the first-line phase 3 (RASolute 303) and the phase 1/2 remain open. The load-bearing constraint for this patient is staging: both the EAP and 303 require confirmed metastatic disease, and 303 additionally requires consent within 6 weeks of the metastatic diagnosis, so the outreach call has to be teed up before the biopsy result lands, not after.
regulatory_status: Investigational; NDA accepted for FDA review July 2026 (previously treated metastatic PDAC), Breakthrough Therapy and Orphan Drug designations, FDA national priority voucher; FDA-authorized expanded access protocol active since May 2026

trials.notes: EAP inclusion requires metastatic PDAC, a prior line that was fluoropyrimidine- or gemcitabine-based, and inability to enroll in a daraxonrasib trial. Whether adjuvant FOLFIRINOX with recurrence at 4 months counts as the qualifying prior line is a protocol question to put to the sponsor; prior Whipple is explicitly allowed. Physician-initiated requests only.

trials.indication: first-line metastatic PDAC, daraxonrasib with or without gemcitabine/nab-paclitaxel (RASolute 303)
trials.title: Study of Daraxonrasib and Daraxonrasib + GnP as First-line Treatment in Patients With Metastatic Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma
trials.notes: Requires metastatic diagnosis within 6 weeks of consent and no prior systemic therapy in the metastatic setting; this patient's adjuvant-only history fits the 1L definition. Practically, the site call should happen the week staging confirms metastatic disease, because screening plus consent has to finish inside the 6-week clock.

trials.title: Study of RMC-6236 in Patients With Advanced Solid Tumors Harboring Specific Mutations in RAS
trials.notes: US-only site list; enrolls RAS G12 tumors including G12R after standard therapy.

trials.title: Study of RAS(ON) Inhibitors in Patients With Gastrointestinal Solid Tumors
trials.notes: Some subprotocols are G12D-restricted; ask which combination arms accept G12R before screening.

trials.title: Phase 3 Study of Daraxonrasib (RMC-6236) in Patients With Previously Treated Metastatic Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma (PDAC)
trials.notes: The positive registrational trial (mOS 13.2 vs 6.6 months); closed to enrollment, listed for context only.

manufacturer.notes: EAP requests must come from a licensed treating physician; the company does not accept patient or caregiver requests directly. Phone and email are verbatim from the sponsor's registry records.

payer_access_notes: Drug is supplied free under the EAP. Press reporting in June 2026 (STAT) described demand outstripping the program's early capacity, so expect a queue and ask the sponsor about realistic start timelines.
next_steps: Before the biopsy result returns, have the oncologist identify the nearest RASolute 303 site (site list on NCT07491445) and pre-alert them, so consent can happen inside the 6-week window if staging reads metastatic.

If 303 does not fit (locally recurrent rather than metastatic disease, slot unavailability, or the team prefers monotherapy), the physician emails medinfo@revmed.com to open an EAP request under NCT07573215.
Ask the same contact whether the phase 1/2 (NCT05379985) or a G12R-accepting RASolve 101 arm (NCT06445062) has nearer-term slots.
Clarify with the sponsor whether adjuvant FOLFIRINOX with recurrence at 4 months satisfies the EAP's prior-line requirement.
geographic_scope: EAP is US-only (physician-submitted); RASolute 303 sites in US, Japan, Australia; phase 1/2 US-only
notes: The highest-value access finding in this case: an approved-track drug with a formal, currently available expanded-access protocol in exactly this disease.

access_summary: Investigational and G12D-selective, so its open phase 3 does not read on a G12R tumor. Kept on the ledger to document the allele gate rather than as a usable route.

trials.indication: first-line metastatic PDAC with KRAS G12D

next_steps: No action; the allele does not match. Daraxonrasib is the Revolution Medicines route for G12R.

access_summary: First-in-human trial explicitly lists KRAS G12R among eligible mutations, and its PDAC expansion counts adjuvant chemotherapy with recurrence inside 6 months as a prior line, which matches this patient's course exactly. IV administration also sidesteps post-Whipple oral-absorption questions. The constraint is that this is dose escalation, so slots and dose levels move week to week.

next_steps: Call the Astellas trial line (800-888-7704, Astellas.registration@astellas.com) to ask which US sites are enrolling and whether the PDAC expansion is open at the current dose level.
Confirm the recurrence is documented as locally advanced unresectable or metastatic before screening.

access_summary: The registry lists eligible mutations as G12A, G12C, G12D, G12S, and G12V. G12R is not on the list, so despite the pan-KRAS label this trial does not currently take this patient. The dossier keeps it as the cautionary example that pan-KRAS programs need codon-level checking.

next_steps: Email clinicaltrials@kestreltherapeutics.com to confirm G12R enrollment and site openings.
If daraxonrasib is the chosen first move, note this trial's prior-RAS-inhibitor exclusion when planning sequence.

The one recruiting trial is an MSK perioperative study in newly diagnosed resectable disease, which this patient's recurrent course does not fit. Net: the mechanism covers G12R, but there is no open door today for a recurrent patient.

Flag the on-treatment biopsy requirement against the vascular-invasion anatomy when the EUS team weighs in.

access_summary: FDA- and EMA-approved for CLDN18.2-positive (75% or more at 2+/3+) HER2-negative gastric/GEJ adenocarcinoma, so a US oncologist can mechanically prescribe it off-label in PDAC today. The evidence and the assay both cut against doing so: the GLEAM phase 2 in PDAC missed its primary OS endpoint (13.7 vs 13.6 months), and this tumor's 60% staining sits below the label-defining cutoff, so expect payer denial and little support from the data. Astellas' early-access program (NCT06048081) is gastric/GEJ-only with US enrollment closed, so it adds nothing here.

access_summary: Approved, but not anywhere this patient can reach: China's NMPA approved satri-cel in June 2026 for CLDN18.2-positive gastric/GEJ cancer after two prior lines, the first CAR-T approval in a solid tumor. If the panel comes back BRCA- or PALB2-positive, the realistic shape is off-label maintenance after a response to a new platinum-containing line, argued case-by-case with the payer. Captured now so the pathway is ready the day the germline result lands.

access_summary: The biomarker fit is the best in the whole CLDN18.2 file, and the honest verdict is still that a US patient cannot get this drug. The only trial is a 12-patient investigator-initiated dose escalation at a single Shanghai center (Fudan University Shanghai Cancer Center), with 2 to 6 treatment cycles after a 68Ga-PET gate, meaning months of care inside the Chinese health system. Single-center Chinese IITs at this scale do not have a mechanism for enrolling foreign patients: consent, insurance, safety follow-up, and China's human-genetic-resources rules all assume local residents, and nothing on the record suggests the sponsor has built an exception. Stated travel willingness does not bridge that; this is the satri-cel situation one stage earlier, minus the approval.

notes: Decision-relevant class finding: a live registry query this run found exactly three CLDN18.2 radioconjugate studies worldwide (this one, IR199 at Huashan, and an imaging-only immunoPET study NCT06602037), all in China. No Western company has a CLDN18.2 radioligand in the clinic or a posted plan for one; the closest Western-visible work is academic preclinical (a 131I-zolbetuximab mouse study). So the modality best matched to this tumor's expression pattern currently has no reachable door at all.

access_summary: Not a route for this patient, twice over. First, the same reachability wall as SNA040: a 10-patient investigator-initiated study at one Shanghai hospital (Huashan), with no mechanism for foreign enrollment. Second, even for a local patient this is not treatment: the primary endpoint is biodistribution and dosimetry from a single administration, so it answers an imaging-physics question rather than offering a therapy course. It matters to this dossier as proof the CLDN18.2 radioconjugate class has a second independent clinical program, and for nothing else yet.
